messages.subject: Starting with GGIR
messages.body_plain:
Hello Vincent,

Thank you for the great work you have invested in the GGIR package.

I use R a regular basis but just starting with GENEActiv sleep files. The files are collecting data over 15 days and are quite large.

When I type a very simple command to inspect the file I get the following message:

library(GGIR)

> dataf <- "C:/projects/diachron/data/6110001_032083_2016-08-05 09-30-05.bin"
> insp <- g.inspectfile(dataf)
Warning messages:
1: In readLines(binfile, 300) : line 27 appears to contain an embedded nul
2: In readLines(binfile, 300) : line 28 appears to contain an embedded nul
3: In readLines(binfile, 300) : line 29 appears to contain an embedded nul
4: In readLines(binfile, 300) : line 30 appears to contain an embedded nul
5: In readLines(binfile, 300) : line 39 appears to contain an embedded nul
6: In readLines(binfile, 300) : line 45 appears to contain an embedded nul
7: In scan(fc, skip = sk, what = "", n = 2, sep = ":", quiet = TRUE) :
  embedded nul(s) found in input

It looks like I have some kind of encoding issue since these lines correspond to the presence signs "caret at" in the bin file as seen in the VI editor.

any idea ?

Thanks in advance, best regards

Jean-Marc Theler

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Starting with GGIR
messages.body_plain:
Hello Jean-Marc,
This warning seems to be related to R package GENEAread. GGIR uses
package GENEAread to read the binary accelerometer data.
To be honest I usually ignore this warning as the data is loaded and
it looks normal, but you are right that it would be good if someone
could investigate this.
Thanks
Vincent

messages.subject: Error with Log
messages.body_plain:
Hi Vincent,

I am attempting to score data from Actigraph accelerometers that were worn 24 hours per day for 7 days. I have a sleep log indicating bed times and wake times in the format discussed in the manual (no date, time only) saved as a csv file. However, I'm getting an error saying that the log cannot be read, permission is denied.

Do you have suggestions?

Thank you,

- Jonathan Kurka

messages.subject: Non-wear time detected
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Any of you know if is there any way to get a report of the non-wear periods detected with GGIR package? I need it to corroborate if the periods detected are similar to the periods reported by participants.

Thank you in advance!

Best,
Jairo

messages.body_plain:
Hi Jairo,
This is stored in rout, see tutorial on g.impute function for more informaiton.
When using g.shell.GGIR the values of rout are stored in the milestone data (.RData) files that come out of part2.
Vincent

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Non-wear time detected
messages.body_plain:
Thank you Vincent.

Another doubt related. I defined window sizes as default (5, 900, 3600). So, I expected data to be imputed just in case that window3 is reached, I mean, if the algorithm detects 1 hour of non-wear time, then this period is imputed. But looking at rout, I've seen some periods imputed of 15 min, i.e. window2. So my question is, Are non-wear detection and imputation done based on window2 or window3 length?

Thank you again, your help is very appreciated.

messages.subject: Part 2 error message "Error in if (firstmidnighti == 1) { : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed"
messages.subject_clean: Part 2 error message "Error in if (firstmidnighti == 1) { : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed"
messages.body_plain:
Hi Vincent (and everyone),

Thank you for all your work in developing GGIR package.

I work as a statistician at the University of Utah, and I am on a study of using GGIR.

I tried to run g.shell.GGIR function on 1 week accelerator data by setting and using the following codes, and I got an error message “Error in if (firstmidnighti == 1) { : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed” in part 2. But my data did start from the midnight. Could you please help me understand and adjust the error?

out=g.shell.GGIR(

#-------------------------------

# General parameters

#-------------------------------

mode=mode,

datadir=datadir,

outputdir=outputdir,

studyname=studyname,

f0=f0,

f1=f1,

overwrite = TRUE,

do.imp=TRUE,

idloc=1,

print.filename=FALSE,

storefolderstructure = FALSE,

#-------------------------------

# Part 1 parameters:

#-------------------------------

windowsizes = c(60,300,3600),

do.cal=TRUE,

do.enmo = TRUE,

do.anglez=TRUE,

chunksize=1,

printsummary=TRUE,

#-------------------------------

# Part 2 parameters:

#-------------------------------

strategy = 1,

hrs.del.start = 0,

hrs.del.end = 0,

includedaycrit = 10,

ilevels=c(0, 100.6, 428.8),

mvpathreshold=c(100.6,428.8, 600),

boutcriter = 0,

#-------------------------------

# Part 3 parameters:

#-------------------------------

timethreshold= 5,

anglethreshold=5,

ignorenonwear = TRUE,

#-------------------------------

# Part 4 parameters:

#-------------------------------

excludefirstlast = TRUE,

includenightcrit = 16,

def.noc.sleep = c(21, 9),

relyonsleeplog = FALSE,

#-----------------------------------

# Report generation

#-------------------------------

do.report = c(2,4)

)

   g.shell.GGIR {GGIR} by Vincent van Hees

________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________

Part 2

 1

Error in if (firstmidnighti == 1) { :

  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

Thanks in advance, best regards

Qian Ding
